stories.title: Get to Know the Broker: Jonathan Stein of Douglas Elliman
stories.excerpt: For Jonathan Stein, the best is yet to come. Stein, 43, joined the real estate game in 2015 after spending time in the private equity space and then going on the road with his best friend’s rock band, Phantogram, as the tour manager. Now, he runs the Jonathan Stein Team at Douglas Elliman. Stein oversees a group of eight brokers at the firm, which has worked on deals ranging from $1 million to over $15 million. When former New York Mets and current Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Zack Wheeler needed to sell his SoHo penthouse at 73 Wooster Street, Stein and team member Gavin Shiminski stepped in, helping the major leaguer sell the unit for $26 million. It was one of the five largest sales in New York City in July. The road to such a successful real estate career wasn’t easy, but Stein said real estate is an amalgamation of his favorite things: design, architecture, mixing different personalities, and working well with people. “I got into real estate the old fashioned way — my life blew up and I needed a new career,” he said. “I was waiting tables at a buddy’s restaurant looking for what was going to come next. A friend suggested real estate and I loved the idea.” Commercial Observer caught up with Stein in August for “Get to Know the Broker,” a series where we connect with residential brokers to learn more about what makes them tick. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: What has been the biggest deal of your career? Jonathan Stein: I haven’t done it yet. Check back next year. What is your career Everest? Doing my own development project! What’s something you think people would be surprised to learn about you? I grew up on a farm in a town of 170 people. We raised cattle and pigs, and I showed pigs in 4-H as a kid to help earn money for college. What’s your go-to takeout order? Sushi from my neighborhood omakase spot. What TV show are you currently binging? “All Creatures Great and Small.” What is your silliest pet peeve? When

Stein oversees an eight-person team handling deals from $1M to $15M. The article is a career profile with no bearing on development underwriting or market fundamentals.

stories.title: Rejection and Change Are Constants in Residential Brokerage. Adapt.
stories.excerpt: When I decided to get my real estate license, it’s safe to say I had no idea what I was in for. The perception of real estate agents is not the reality. A lot of people assume it’s about the money, but, for me, it’s really all about building and nurturing relationships. I’ve closed many deals by focusing on what was best for my clients, even when it required extra flexibility and problem-solving on my end. I realized early on that half the battle was just being available and accessible, and that building trust and transparency from the first call is key. As a young agent in the industry, I didn’t come into real estate with many connections. Most of my circle wasn’t ready to purchase a home or hire an agent for a rental. I had to find my own path, generating leads organically. But, as a young agent, I was extremely motivated to do so, and I was ready to adapt if needed. Mackenzie Kyle. PHOTO: Courtesy Platinum Properties One of my first deals was in the Financial District. My client’s mom found my profile on RentHop and called me out of the blue. We spoke about her search, and she asked if I could show an apartment in an hour. I lived an hour away from the building at this time, so I quickly rushed over. After a day of last-minute tours, I helped them find an apartment they loved. Their daughter was fresh out of school, and they were nervous about her moving to New York City, but, with my guidance and reassurance, they felt confident that the apartment was the right choice. I didn’t know this deal would jump-start my entire career, but it did. Not only do I still have an amazing relationship with these clients and have helped them find multiple homes, I was also connected with so many amazing referral clients from them because of the superior level of service that I provided. stories.title: The Broker’s Guide to Winning Certainty in Bridge Lending

stories.title: Podcast: Using AI to Make Better CRE Acquisition & Underwriting Decisions
stories.excerpt: Steven Song is the founder and CEO of Diald, an AI-powered decision intelligence platform for commercial real estate. Before founding Diald, Steven worked on both the investing and development sides of real estate, and built his career across architecture and urban planning, training at Carnegie Mellon and the University of Pennsylvania. He was a founding principal at SCAAA, a global strategy, planning, and design firm, and is a partner at Axle Companies, a family office focused on real estate investment and social impact ventures. Steven is based in Los Angeles. stories.title: Machine Investment Group Closes Second Fund at Hard Cap of $350M
stories.excerpt: Machine Investment Group, LP, a New York City-based real estate investment platform focused on opportunistic, distressed and special situations across the U.S., reached the final close of Machine Real Estate Fund II, the firm’s second flagship investment vehicle. Fund II reached its $350 million hard cap in primary commitments and has raised an additional $120 million in co-investments to date. Fund II received support from a diverse group of new and returning institutional investors, including public and private pension funds, endowments, foundations, family offices and private investors. Fund II exceeded Machine’s debut fund, Machine Real Estate Fund I, which closed in 2022 with $246 million in primary commitments and $208 million in co-investments. “We are humbled by the support of our investment partners, including both returning Fund I investors and a number of new institutional relationships, which allowed us to reach our hard cap for Fund II,” said Eric Rosenthal, co-founder and managing partner of Machine Investment Group. “Reaching our hard cap in what continues to be a challenging fundraising environment, particularly for middle market managers pursuing a diversified strategy, is a milestone we do not take for granted.” Representative Fund II investments include a special situations powered land investment in Pennsylvania, a distressed 539-unit residential property in downtown San Jose, a 229-unit senior housing property on Long Island acquired out of a distressed situation, a recently developed 1.3 million square foot industrial park in Phoenix and a strategic capital investment in a publicly traded company being repositioned as a powered land and data center development platform. bullets: Machine Investment Group closes Fund II at $350M primary, $120M co-invest; hard cap reached.

stories.summary: Machine Investment Group, a NYC-based real estate platform focused on opportunistic and distressed deals, closed its second flagship fund at a $350M hard cap plus $120M in co-investments, exceeding the 2022 debut fund's $246M. The fund drew support from institutional investors including pension funds, endowments, and family offices, reaching its target despite a difficult fundraising landscape for middle-market managers pursuing diversified strategies.
stories.impact: Signals sustained institutional capital appetite for value-add and distressed multifamily and mixed-use plays across U.S. despite near-term rate uncertainty. Larger second close suggests confidence in deal flow and sponsor returns; competitive pressure likely for acquisition targets in secondary/tertiary markets where Machine typically operates, potentially pushing cap rates tighter or valuations higher in those segments.

stories.title: Jamison CEO Jaime Lee Joins Kennedy Wilson as Senior Managing Director
stories.excerpt: Kennedy Wilson said Wednesday that Jaime Lee has joined the firm as senior managing director of capital markets and real estate investments. Most recently CEO of Los Angeles-based Jamison, Lee joins Kennedy Wilson as the firm continues to expand its investment management platform and deepen relationships with institutional and private capital partners.   In her new role, Lee will help lead capital formation initiatives, strengthen relationships with institutional investors and strategic partners, and help drive investment opportunities across Kennedy Wilson’s global real estate platform.  “Jaime brings an exceptional combination of investment expertise, operational experience and longstanding relationships across both the private and public sectors,” said William McMorrow, chairman and CEO of Kennedy Wilson. “As we continue to grow our investment management platform and expand our capital formation capabilities, Jaime’s proven ability to build partnerships, identify opportunities and navigate complex transactions will be invaluable.” Lee joins Kennedy Wilson following more than 20 years at Jamison, where she helped transform the company into one of Southern California’s largest privately held real estate owners and developers.  The post Jamison CEO Jaime Lee Joins Kennedy Wilson as Senior Managing Director appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Jaime Lee, ex-CEO of LA-based Jamison (20+ years tenure), joins Kennedy Wilson.
Lee hired as Senior Managing Director of capital markets and real estate investments.

stories.summary: Jaime Lee, longtime CEO of Los Angeles-based Jamison, joined Kennedy Wilson as Senior Managing Director of Capital Markets and Real Estate Investments. Lee brings two decades of operational and investment experience and will lead capital formation initiatives and investor relations for Kennedy Wilson's global platform. No transaction data or deal specifics are disclosed.
stories.impact: Talent migration from established LA developer to larger institutional platform signals consolidation of deal-sourcing and capital-raising functions. Lee's LA and Jamison networks may accelerate KW's acquisition velocity and LP access in West Coast multifamily, potentially lifting competition for development-stage and value-add assets in SoCal and secondary Western markets.

stories.title: Developer Iadisernia Lands Mezz Loan to Finish Hallandale, Fla., Condo Tower
stories.excerpt: More than a year after landing a $112 million loan to complete a mixed-use project in Hallandale Beach, Fla., developer Giuseppe Iadisernia has secured yet more debt. Cottonwood Group supplied a $50 million mezzanine loan for a 250-unit condo tower within the 10-acre Oasis mixed-use development at 1000 East Hallandale Beach Boulevard, about a mile west of the beach, the L.A.-based lender announced Wednesday. Construction is expected to be completed next year. Emile Schachter’s WD Capital Group brokered the debt. A representative for the lender has yet to provide figures regarding condo sales. Last year, S3 Capital had provided the $112 million construction loan for the 25-story tower, considered the last phase of the mixed-use broader development. Prices range from $580,000 and $3.5 million. Just last month, the first condo tower, also a 250-unit, 25-story high-rise, secured a temporary certificate of occupancy up to the 12th floor. The development includes a commercial portion with about 35,000 square feet of office space and 60,000 square feet of retail space, which was completed in 2024. Since the pandemic, when northerners flocked to Florida, Hallandale has been going upscale. In 2024, Witkoff and PPG Development nabbed a $273 million construction loan for a 20-story condo and hotel building within their exclusive Shell Bay golf country club. But some projects have struggled. In March, Monroe Capital sued PPG Development’s Ari Pearl and the principals of BH3 over a $70 million loan tied to Hallandale Beach Residences, The Real Deal reported. The lender alleged the developer stopped making payments in February. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Developer Iadisernia secures $50M mezzanine loan from Cottonwood Group for Hallandale condo tower.
250-unit, 25-story luxury condo project at Oasis mixed-use (10 acres); prices $580K–$3.5M.

stories.summary: Developer Giuseppe Iadisernia obtained a $50M mezzanine loan from Cottonwood Group to complete a 250-unit luxury condo tower at the Oasis mixed-use development in Hallandale Beach, Florida. Unit prices range from $580K to $3.5M. The project follows an earlier $112M construction loan from S3 Capital; the first tower recently achieved a partial certificate of occupancy, with full completion targeted for 2025.
stories.impact: Indicates South Florida condo financing and market remain active despite 2023–2024 rate headwinds; mezzanine layer secured on top of construction debt suggests lender and sponsor confidence in pre-sales and exit. Hallandale beachfront demand and pricing power justify layered capital structure, signaling continued investor appetite for Florida luxury multifamily/mixed-use conversions. Watch condo pre-sales and absorption rates as proxy for South Florida rental demand in 2025.

stories.title: Century 21 Redevelopment Adds Burlington, National Grocer to Tenant Roster
stories.excerpt: MCB Real Estate, an institutional commercial real estate investment management firm and developer with nationwide holdings, and Osiris Ventures, an urban retail-focused investment firm, have secured leases with two major retail brands at Century Marketplace, the $130-million mixed-use redevelopment of the 14-lot Century 21 department store assemblage at 458 86th St. in Brooklyn’s Bay Ridge neighborhood. A national grocery anchor has signed a lease at the property, becoming the first national grocer to serve the immediate Southwest Brooklyn trade area. National designer-discount retailer Burlington has also signed on, and together the two leases total 60,112 square feet. With these additions, the 120,000-square-foot Century Marketplace is now 65% pre-leased. “Century Marketplace demonstrates MCB Real Estate’s ability to execute complex structuring while delivering high quality, attractive retail to dense markets,” said MCB principal Drew Gorman. “By bringing together a nationally recognized specialty grocery anchor, and top national retailers like Burlington, we are reigniting a well-known commercial corridor and unlocking long term value for Southwest Brooklyn.” The post Century 21 Redevelopment Adds Burlington, National Grocer to Tenant Roster appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MCB Real Estate and Osiris Ventures secure leases for Burlington and national grocer at Century Marketplace.

stories.summary: MCB Real Estate and Osiris Ventures announced leases with national grocery and discount retailer Burlington at Century Marketplace, a $130M mixed-use redevelopment of the Century 21 department store site at 458 86th Street in Brooklyn's Bay Ridge neighborhood. The 120,000-square-foot project is now 65% pre-leased, with the two new tenants accounting for 60,112 square feet. The grocery anchor is the first national grocer to serve Southwest Brooklyn's immediate trade area.
stories.impact: Signals retail stabilization and foot-traffic recovery in secondary Brooklyn submarkets; grocery anchor fills void and anchors urban mixed-use development. Strong pre-lease velocity (65%) at $130M property suggests cap rates compressing on proven mixed-use/retail platforms; reduced downside risk attracts institutional capital. Grocery anchor in underserved Southwest Brooklyn may trigger residential demand lift if the property drives population concentration, though residential rents not discussed.

stories.title: Multi-Tenant Corona del Mar Retail Sells Above Asking Price
stories.excerpt: Coastal Commercial and Marcus & Millichap arranged the $13.7-million sale of 2515 E. Coast Highway, a prominent multi-tenant retail property located in Corona del Mar. The transaction was represented by Nathan Holthouser of Coastal Commercial and Ron Duong of Marcus & Millichap. The offering generated significant interest from the Orange County investment community, attracting more than 10 offers and multiple rounds of competitive bidding. Prospective buyers consisted primarily of high-net-worth private investors with ties to Orange County. Ultimately, the property sold for $700,000 above its asking price. “The response to this offering was exceptional, but I think sophisticated investors quickly recognized the underlying value of the real estate,” said Holthouser. “You have incredible frontage along Pacific Coast Highway, approximately 20 onsite parking spaces — which is extremely difficult to replicate in Corona del Mar — and a collection of mostly smaller commercial spaces that lend themselves well to maximizing rents over time.” The post Multi-Tenant Corona del Mar Retail Sells Above Asking Price appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Multi-tenant retail property in Corona del Mar, CA sold for $13.7M, $700K above asking.
10+ offers and multiple bidding rounds from high-net-worth Orange County investors.
Strong demand for limited parking and prominent PCH frontage; small-format spaces support rent growth.
stories.summary: A multi-tenant retail property at 2515 E. Coast Highway in Corona del Mar sold for $13.7M, exceeding asking price by $700K. The sale attracted over 10 offers and competitive bidding from high-net-worth Orange County investors. The property features ~20 onsite parking spaces (scarce in Corona del Mar) and smaller commercial spaces conducive to rent upside.
stories.impact: Indicates strong Orange County retail investor appetite and scarce supply of waterfront commercial with parking; pricing power and scarcity premium for prime coastal CA retail. Not directly material to multifamily development but signals broader OC investor confidence and capital availability that could elevate mixed-use development competition and land values in premium coastal submarkets.

stories.title: Walker & Dunlop Arranges Financing for Stamford Residential Conversion
stories.excerpt: Walker & Dunlop has arranged a $74.5-million loan for the acquisition and redevelopment of The Caspian, a luxury development in Stamford, CT. The Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory team led by Aaron Appel, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Sean Reimer, Dustin Stolly, Jordan Casella and Stanley Cayre arranged the financing, provided by an affiliate of Apollo Global Management, on behalf of Sun Homes and Hudson Bay Capital. Located at 68-70 Seaview Ave., the project will transform an existing seven-story, 241,000-square-foot waterfront office building into 63 luxury condominium residences featuring a mix of one-, two-, and three-bedroom homes along with townhome residences. Amenities include a grand lobby, indoor and outdoor amenity spaces, private rooftop terraces, a 57-slip marina and structured parking. “Fairfield and Westchester counties remain highly supply-constrained residential markets, particularly for new waterfront product given limited developable shoreline and complex entitlement processes,” said Jonathan Schwartz. “The Caspian is uniquely positioned to address that supply-demand imbalance with a best-in-class luxury offering in one of the region’s most desirable waterfront locations. We’re grateful to Sun Homes, Hudson Bay Capital, and Apollo Global Management for their partnership in bringing this vision forward.” The conversations behind tomorrow’s apartment deals happen at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Connect with the capital sources, owners, developers, and brokers driving multifamily investment. Learn more and reserve your seat at www.connectapts2026.com. bullets: Walker & Dunlop arranges $74.5M loan (Apollo affiliate) for Stamford waterfront residential conversion.

stories.summary: Walker & Dunlop arranged a $74.5M loan from an Apollo Global Management affiliate for The Caspian, a luxury conversion of a 241,000-square-foot waterfront office building into 63 condos in Stamford, Connecticut. The project includes one-, two-, and three-bedroom residences, townhomes, amenities, a 57-slip marina, and structured parking. Lender commentary emphasizes supply constraints in Fairfield/Westchester, particularly for waterfront product given entitlement complexity and limited shoreline.
stories.impact: Signals sustained capital availability for office-to-residential conversions in supply-constrained coastal Connecticut markets; waterfront product commands institutional debt at scale. Stamford's supply squeeze and entitlement barriers create opening for pre-entitled or entitled development; luxury pricing and mix support debt service on mid-size projects. Developer-friendly lending environment for conversion plays in Northeast submarkets; likely to accelerate office-to-resi conversions in Westchester, making ground-up development harder to underwrite vs. conversion arbitrage.
